checks.s: The memo identifies at least ten distinct categories of SOW terms that deviate from the firm's internal contracting policy.

The memo identifies deviations in all of these categories: liability cap, consequential damages, indemnification scope, IP ownership, payment terms, termination for convenience, warranty period/scope, regulatory/data-handling compliance, personnel replacement and/or liquidated damages, and rate discount.

The memo states that the client's proposed aggregate liability cap is 50% of fees paid in the trailing 12-month period and that this is below the internal policy floor of 100% of fees paid in the trailing 12-month period.
The memo explains the commercial or legal exposure created by setting the proposed liability cap at half the policy-required minimum.
The memo identifies the client's proposed consequential damages provision as allowing recovery for data breaches, beyond the policy-permitted exceptions.
The memo identifies the client's proposed consequential damages provision as allowing recovery for regulatory fines, beyond the policy-permitted exceptions.
The memo identifies a carve-out for project delays exceeding 45 calendar days in the client's proposed consequential damages provision and states that it is beyond the policy-permitted exceptions.
The memo states that the firm's internal policy permits consequential damages carve-outs only for breaches of confidentiality and IP indemnity obligations.

The memo identifies that the client requires the Firm to indemnify against all third-party claims arising from the Firm's performance of services and notes that this is broader than the policy-permitted scope.
The memo identifies that the proposed indemnification scope includes claims by regulatory authorities related to data handling.
The memo states that the firm's internal policy limits indemnification to third-party IP infringement claims and breaches of confidentiality.

The memo identifies that the client demands ownership of all custom-developed deliverables, including derivative works incorporating the Firm's pre-existing frameworks, while the Firm retains only a non-exclusive license to its own pre-existing IP as embedded.

The memo states that under the firm's internal policy, all pre-existing IP and reusable frameworks remain Firm property and the client receives only a perpetual, non-exclusive license to deliverables.
The memo flags the risk that the proposed IP ownership terms threaten the Firm's reusable IP portfolio or its ability to use its pre-existing frameworks in other engagements.
The memo identifies that the client insists on Net 60 payment terms, deviating from the policy standard of Net 30 days from invoice date.
The memo identifies that the client's proposal removes or omits late payment interest and that policy requires late payment interest at 1.5% per month.
The memo identifies that the client proposes 15 calendar days' written notice for termination for convenience, below the policy-required minimum of 30 days' written notice.

The memo identifies that the client's termination-for-convenience proposal excludes payment for non-cancellable third-party costs, although policy requires the client to pay those costs upon termination.
The memo identifies that the client demands a 180-day warranty period from deliverable acceptance, which exceeds the policy-permitted 60-day warranty period.
The memo identifies that the proposed warranty covers performance failures and/or conformance to functional specifications beyond defect correction only, the policy standard.
The memo identifies that the client requires the Firm to warrant ongoing compliance with OCC and FFIEC guidelines applicable to Meridian's technology vendors.
The memo identifies that the client's proposed terms require the Firm to submit to regulatory examination.
The memo states that the firm's internal policy provides that the Firm assumes no regulatory compliance obligations beyond its own standard information security practices.

The memo identifies the client's demand for the right to approve all replacement personnel as a deviation from policy, which gives the client only the right to request replacement with 15 business days' notice.
The memo identifies the client's proposed liquidated damages of $15,000 per incident if a named key person voluntarily departs the engagement within the first 9 months.
The memo states that the firm's internal policy does not permit liquidated damages for attrition or personnel departures.

The memo identifies an approximately 12% discount from the standard blended rate of $324/hour, resulting in a proposed rate of $285/hour, and states that this exceeds the engagement lead's authorized discount authority of 8% without escalation.
The memo gives a numerical measure of how far the discount exceeds the 8% authority, such as a percentage-point overage, a dollar-per-hour difference, or a total-fee impact.
The memo is addressed or directed to the Deal Review Board (DRB) and/or its Chair, Marcus Trelleborg (Chief Commercial Officer).
The memo references the statement of work by the number SOW-2025-0439.
The memo references the governing Master Services Agreement by the number MSA-2022-1187.
The memo identifies the internal contracting policy by the designation CTP-LEGAL-POL-009 or by a recognizable full title.
The memo states that Meridian represents approximately 11% of Crestfield's trailing twelve-month consulting revenue.
The memo states that the proposed engagement is valued at approximately $8,740,000.
The memo makes a clear, affirmative request or recommendation to the Deal Review Board to approve, or approve with conditions, the out-of-policy terms.
The memo references the next DRB session date of July 17, 2025, in connection with the urgency of the approval request.
The memo references the proposed SOW effective date of August 1, 2025, in connection with the urgency of the approval request.
